body.v: Someone is signing up for SwissAlpBank e-banking with this email address. To continue, they need the following verification code: 482 913
This code is valid for 10 minutes. Do not share it with anyone: no SwissAlpBank employee will ever ask you for it.
If you did not make this request, you do not need to do anything. No account can be opened without this code.

hotspots.explain: swissalpbank.example: the bank's exact domain, with no variation.
You asked for nothing. Someone typed in your address, by mistake or hoping to talk the code out of you later. The email is genuine, but you were not expecting it.
"Do not share it with anyone": every genuine service writes this. If someone asks you for this code afterwards, they are a scammer.
No link, nothing to pay, nothing to send back. Doing nothing puts you at no risk.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Read the address, not just the name.
who.answer: SwissAlpBank: the address is on the bank's domain, swissalpbank.example. But you did not ask for this code, so someone else started the sign-up.
choices: A scammer imitating the bank's address
A friend who wants to send you money
cues: Compare the sender address with swissalpbank.example.
Did you start a registration yourself?

emotion.prompt: Which feeling is this email pressing on?
emotion.answer: None. It is a neutral notice, with no threat and no pressure on you.
choices: Fear of losing access to your account
None, it is a calm, neutral notice
cues: Is there a threat or a deadline aimed at you?

ask.prompt: What does it actually want you to do?
ask.answer: Nothing. It shows a code and asks you to keep it to yourself.
choices: Click a link and sign in
Nothing, except keep the code to yourself
cues: Is there a link, a payment or a request for a reply?

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Nothing to do. If these codes keep arriving, open the SwissAlpBank app yourself or call the number on the back of your card.
choices: Reply with the code to cancel the sign-up
If it happens again, open the app yourself
Pass the code to a relative so they can check
cues: A channel you control is one you open yourself, not one the email gives you.

actions.label: Keep the code to yourself and ignore the email
actions.consequence: Nothing happens. Without the code, nobody can open an account with your address.

actions.label: Give the code to someone who calls or writes to you asking for it
actions.consequence: With that code, they finish the sign-up in your name. A real bank never asks you for it.

actions.label: If it happens again, open the SwissAlpBank app yourself and alert the bank
actions.consequence: The bank sees the attempts and can block them. You were in control the whole time.

actions.label: Reply to ask what is going on
actions.consequence: Nobody reads what arrives at a no-reply address. No harm done, but you learn nothing either.

attacker_reveal: I had nothing to do with this one: the bank's domain, no link, no request. A genuine email can still turn up uninvited. What I would want is the code, so if anyone asks you for it, even in the bank's name, keep it.
